tagline.text: A 1905 American-era lighthouse above the western sea, and a sunset spot

location.label: Location
location.text: Cape Beach Road, Barangay Patar, Bolinao, Pangasinan

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–900 (per person, on-site for one day, excluding round-trip transport from Manila)

children.text: Cape Bolinao Lighthouse, built in 1905, stands on a cliff in Barangay Patar at the western tip of Pangasinan. You cannot enter the tower, but from outside you can enjoy the South China Sea, the ruined former administration building and the Patar sunset together.

Cape Bolinao Lighthouse stands on Punta Piedra Point in Barangay Patar, Bolinao, Pangasinan, on the northwest coast of Luzon. Set on a high cape facing the South China Sea, it has long guided ships traveling up and down the Philippine west coast. It lies around 16.3072° N, 119.7856° E, at the western end of the municipality,
about 15 km
in a straight line from the center of Bolinao town.
The lighthouse was built in 1905 and first lit in 1906. It is said to have been built jointly by three engineers, one each from the United States, Britain and the Philippines. The tower is about
tall, and the light sits about
above sea level. Because of that elevation, it is known as the second-highest lighthouse in the Philippines after Cape Bojeador. It is often mentioned as a pair with the American-era
Cape Bojeador Lighthouse
in Ilocos.

The original third-order lens apparatus was imported from England and the lantern from France, and Filipino mechanics later built a near-identical replica. The light burned kerosene for many years before it was connected to the electric grid in the 1980s. The owner is the Philippine Coast Guard. It is described as a locally managed heritage site, but it is hard to confirm today that it still works as a navigation aid.

The first thing travelers should know is that you cannot go inside the tower and climb its 140-step spiral staircase. Instead, the way to enjoy the site is to look up at the whole tower from outside the fence and in the grounds, take photos at the ruins of the former administration building right next to it, and watch the sun sink over the western horizon at dusk. It fits well as a stop of
1–2 hours
combined with other Bolinao sights.
The white cylindrical tower rising between blue sky and sea is the main sight here. The tower is about
tall, and looking up from the base makes a good composition. Entry to the tower is closed, so you will have to be content with viewing it from outside.

blocks.title: Ruins of the former administration building

children.text: Right beside the tower, the administrative building used by the lighthouse keepers stands in ruins. The collapsed walls and window frames pair well with the lighthouse and make a popular photo spot. There is a risk of collapse, so it is best not to go inside.

On the cape, the sea opens to the west with nothing in the way. On clear days you can see the line where the water shifts from deep blue to turquoise. It is often windy, so take care that hats and glasses do not blow away.
The coast here faces west, and the Patar area is known as a top sunset spot. Arrive about
1 hour
before sunset to watch the light change. The grounds may close early, so check in advance that opening hours match sunset.

What defines this lighthouse is its story: an English lens, a French lantern and engineers from three countries. From the kerosene days to the connection to the electric grid, it is far more interesting to walk around while thinking about more than 100 years of guiding ships.
The area around the lighthouse leads on to the Patar coast, and Patar Beach and a rocky shoreline are within walking distance. If you are staying in Patar, it makes a good sunset stroll.
Have breakfast in Bolinao town (poblacion) and hire a tricycle. In 2017 the going rate to Patar was around
one way, so ask for the current price before bargaining.
Visit one of the Bolinao Falls first. If you pay the environmental fee, it can sometimes be used at several attractions, so keep the receipt.
Have lunch in town or in Patar and rest for a while. The midday sun is strong, so avoid walking outdoors for long at this hour.
Arrive at the lighthouse grounds and photograph the tower, the ruins and the sea view. There is little shade, so bring water and a hat.
Walk to Patar Beach or the rocky shoreline to watch the sunset.
Return to town or your lodging by tricycle before it gets dark.
Some sources say the grounds are open roughly from 8:00 to 17:00, but this is hard to verify officially. If you plan to stay until sunset, be sure to ask about closing time at the entrance.

items.title: Overnight in Patar
items.subtitle: Walk to the lighthouse and sunset

children.text: If you took the overnight bus from Manila, you arrive in Bolinao early in the morning. Even before check-in, leave your bags and have breakfast.
Swim, snorkel or relax at Patar Beach.
Stroll slowly toward the lighthouse along Cape Beach Road, the coastal road of Patar.
Look around the lighthouse and the former administration building and take photos.
Watch the sunset from the nearby rocky shoreline. Check on site whether there is an entrance fee.
Have a seafood dinner near your lodging.
From the Cubao terminal in Quezon City, Manila, direct buses to Bolinao run, including Victory Liner, Five Star and Dagupan Bus. The trip takes about
6 hours
As of 2017, the Victory Liner one-way fare was about ₱459, so many operators have raised fares since. Check the current fare at the terminal.
If you leave around midnight, you reach Bolinao town around 6:00 in the morning. If buses are full, take a bus bound for Alaminos, get off there, and continue about
1 hour
more by bus or van.
Bus schedules and terminal locations change often, so check the operator's announcements before you leave.
Take NLEX, SCTEX and TPLEX in turn, exit at Ramos or Paniqui, and head west across Pangasinan. The drive takes about
5–6 hours
Search for Cape Bolinao Lighthouse on Google Maps and it will guide you to the end of Cape Beach Road in Patar. The last stretch is a narrow coastal road, so drive slowly.
Check on site whether parking is available in the grounds and what it costs.

items.title: From Bolinao town to the lighthouse

children.text: Bolinao has no jeepneys, and tricycles are the main transport. From town to Patar it was around
one way per vehicle (up to 4 people), but that is a 2017 figure and it may cost more now.
A full-day hire was around
in 2017, with entrance and parking fees extra. Hiring one by the day is convenient if you combine the lighthouse, the falls and the beach.
Many reviews say that if you stay in Patar, you can walk from Patar Beach to the lighthouse.
Bolinao has no airport. Fly into Manila (MNL) or Clark (CRK), then continue by land.
Plan your schedule allowing for the time it takes to get from the airport to a bus terminal in Manila.
The west coast of Pangasinan is generally in the dry season from November to May, when the sea is clear and sunsets are likely. Go in the late afternoon on a clear day for the best photos.

June to October is the rainy season and may bring typhoons, so waves are high and the weather changes a lot. In this period, check the forecast and local government announcements and leave some slack in your plans.

There is almost no lodging around the lighthouse itself, and places to stay are clustered along the Patar coast within walking distance. Resorts and guesthouses around Patar Beach fill up early on weekends and holidays, so book soon. In Bolinao town you can also choose an eco-lodge or a small inn.

Food centers on seafood. Stalls at Patar Beach sell snacks and fruit shakes, and there are local restaurants in town. Some places also sell lunch together with a Bolinao river cruise, so ask for the latest prices locally and choose according to your plans.
Go knowing that you cannot enter the tower. Lower your expectations and plan it as a stop for photos from outside, and you will be more satisfied.
The grounds have little shade and are windy. Be sure to bring a hat, sunscreen and water.
If you plan to watch the sunset, arrive between
1–2 hours
before it, and first check at the entrance what time the grounds close.
If you come by tricycle, there may be no ride back, so ask the driver to wait or agree on a round-trip price before you set out.
Reports say an environmental fee receipt is accepted at several attractions, so keep it rather than throwing it away.
If you stay in Patar, you can reach the lighthouse, the beach and the rocky shoreline on foot, which cuts transport costs.
Bring plenty of phone battery. You will take many photos around sunset.
A day trip from Manila is hard, as travel alone takes about
12 hours
round trip. We recommend at least one night.
You cannot enter the tower, and assessments of its upkeep vary by source. Do not go near the inside of the ruined building or the cliff edge.
Official postings for opening hours and fees could not be confirmed. The figures here are based on several travel reviews, so check locally.
It is a cliff-top site, so it is windy and some railings may be low. Take special care when taking photos near the edge.
After sunset there are few streetlights and the roads are dark. Avoid traveling alone after dark.
In the rainy and typhoon season, waves are high and approaching the coast is dangerous. Check the weather forecast.
Some reviews say the surrounding facilities look rundown. It is best not to expect much from the amenities or the restrooms.
In the town side, reachable from the lighthouse by tricycle,
Bolinao
has St. James the Great Church, a museum and seafood restaurants.
A white-sand beach in the same barangay as the lighthouse, good for swimming and snorkeling, and also famous for its sunset. Reviews put the entrance fee at about
Falls 1 to 3 are clustered in Barangay Samang Norte, and reviews put the entrance fee at about
. Life vests are said to be required.
Hundred Islands
on the Alaminos side is a nearby sight that takes more than
1 hour
from Bolinao by bus or van, and it is often added as a follow-on stop.
